Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: throughput-focused onboarding plan

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — NovaProd is excited to move forward. Our main constraint is per-request unit cost while keeping p50 latency under ~150ms for single-turn generation at our typical 512-token sequences. The use case is high-concurrency chat (peak concurrent sessions ~1.2k) with occasional long tails.

Can you propose a short onboarding plan that prioritizes throughput and unit-cost? In particular, we care about:
- batching strategy and expected batch sizes for 512-token median sequences
- KV/prefix caching options to reduce repeated context cost across user sessions
- quantization profiles you recommend by model (we currently evaluate two open models)
- routing policy suggestions for on-demand vs reserved capacity (and any warm pool ideas)

Also share any pieces we need to provide before kickoff (example prompts, traffic profile, and current latency histograms).

Sasha
Sasha Martin
Head of Platform
NovaProd

Hi Sasha — great talking earlier. I sketched a compact onboarding action map that focuses on throughput-first changes we can make during Week 0–2 and the follow-up optimization track. The attached PDF is a concise plan; summary below.

High-level plan (Week 0–2):
1) Discovery (48 hrs): you send a 24–48hr sample of production traffic (prompts + anonymized metadata) and desired SLOs. Also share any peak concurrency windows.
2) Baseline profiling (48–72 hrs): we run a dry-profile on your sample traffic in a staging environment to measure token distribution, sequence-length percentiles, and cold-start latency.
3) Quick wins (72 hrs):
   - Batch tuning: start with a conservative dynamic-batching profile tuned for p50 <= 150ms, target batch sizes 8–16 for 512-token median sequences; we’ll iterate to find the knee.
   - KV/prefix caching: enable prefix caching for session-scoped prompts (expected 10–30% token reduction on median sessions).
   - Routing: route reads through Dedicated pool for steady-state, allow Hosted burst for spiky peaks with automatic fallback to an LR (lower-cost) quantized variant on overload.
   - Quantization: initial recommendation — int8 for the primary model (best latency/cost tradeoff), int4 candidate for long-tail low-accuracy tolerant routes.
4) Implementation (week 2): deploy the batching/caching profiles, set up telemetry dashboards and threshold alerts for p50/p95 latency and token cost.

What we need from you before kickoff:
- 48hr anonymized request sample (prompts + timestamps + route IDs) — preferably JSON (see attachment name novaprod_prompt_samples.json).
- Target latency SLOs (p50/p95) and acceptable quality delta for quantized variants.
- Approx peak concurrency and desired uptime windows.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 11/05 14:00 PT or Fri 11/06 10:00 PT — which works for your engineering and infra leads?

I’ve attached the short action map (redwood_throughput_map_v1.pdf). We’ll bring Monica (CS lead) and Vivek (runtime) to the kickoff to make decisions on quant profiles and routing.

—Camila
Camila Reyes
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Internal: NovaProd onboarding — quick action split (kickoff 14:00 PT)

Team — running internal pre-kickoff checklist and assigning owners before the external call at 14:00 PT. Quick notes and asks:

Context: NovaProd wants throughput-first onboarding, p50 target ~150ms, peak concurrent ~1.2k. They evaluate two open models: "open-llama-x" (preferred quality) and "swift-small" (faster).

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Monica: lead kickoff, align CS scope and user-experience expectations; confirm required SLOs during call and capture acceptance criteria (ETA: today EOD).
- Vivek: prepare a quick profiling runbook and a staging config: propose initial batching profiles (dynamic batching with max_batch 32, target_latency 150ms, starting batch_hint 8) and KV cache TTL suggestions (session-level 10m, cross-session 6h). Also include suggested warm-pool size math for 1.2k concurrency. Bring two quant profiles: int8 baseline, int4 aggressive (owner: vivek, ETA: 90 mins).
- Marissa: prepare cost delta estimates between hosted burst + dedicated steady-state for expected QPS, and a fallback routing policy that demotes to quantized variant when queue depth exceeds threshold. Provide a simple cost/latency table for the call (ETA: 45 mins).

Notes on specifics to discuss:
- Batching: for median 512 tokens, we expect effective batch sizes 10–20 depending on concurrency and arrival patterns. Start conservative to avoid p95 regressions.
- Caching: prioritize prefix caching for multi-turn sessions; recommend conservative cache-keying to avoid cache poisoning.
- Quantization: plan A = int8 on primary model; Plan B = int4 on non-critical routes (e.g., summarization) and as overflow target for bursts. Check if open-llama-x behaves well at int8 (Vivek to confirm).
- Routing policy: Dedicated pool for steady traffic; Hosted burst allowed for spikes with weighted fallback to quantized variant after configured queue threshold. Also discuss a short warm-up policy to pre-warm N instances 5 minutes before predictable high windows.

Please reply inline if any of the suggested owners can’t make the call. I’ll run the kickoff and collate notes for Sasha.

—Camila
